angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 668,429 km at 149.16 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.7042 +/- 0.0126 mas (same row, RUWE 0.92): 149.16 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.9608 +/- 0.0158 solar radii from MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1194 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract): 668,429 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.9835 +/- 0.0298 solar masses from MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1194 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5394 +/- 65 K from MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1194 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1194 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1194.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.466, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
